items.evidence: Notes cover the wheel sensor cost ('The industrial designer flagged the wheel sensor's cost') and the voice-recognition chip email, but do not describe the Industrial Designer presenting the functional components (standard chip, push buttons, wheel sensor). In the transcript the voice chip was raised by the UI designer, not in the ID's presentation.

Notes say 'The UI designer favored a simple layout...' and 'Some buttons on existing remotes were hard to reach', but do not clearly say he presented existing remote controls as models for the interface.
Notes mention a simple layout and thumb reach, but not that the design becomes simpler by dropping the extra buttons of the displayed models.
'The market presentation ranked fancy look and feel first... It reported a trend toward fruit and vegetable forms.'
'It reported a trend toward fruit and vegetable forms. A spongy material was suggested.' and banana with 'spongy cover' chosen.
'The group settled the main concept' and lists the chosen features.

Banana shape, spongy cover, wheel on top, standard battery and chip are stated; 'No decision was made to add voice features.' Lighted buttons are not stated as part of the final design (lighting only discussed, battery concern noted).

'The industrial designer and UI designer were asked to work together on the prototype' and next work includes 'checking the product against user requirements.' Does not name the Project Manager but the instruction is captured.
'The industrial designer and UI designer were asked to work together on the prototype.'
'The next work included ... checking the product against user requirements.'
'The chosen concept was a yellow, banana-shaped remote with a wheel on top and buttons on the side.'
'yellow, banana-shaped remote' and 'The case would have a spongy cover over an inner structure.'
Notes mention a light from the earlier concept and the lighting discussion, but never state that the buttons will be lighted as a decision (PM states buttons are lighted at 20:38).
'The wheel stays despite its higher cost, for ease of use and innovation.'
'banana-shaped remote with a wheel on top'

Notes say 'the selected chip-on-print component' and 'No decision was made to add voice features,' but do not say the standard chip excludes speech recognition. Transcript shows voice was deferred and never revisited, with the prior meeting's no-voice decision standing.
'The design would use a standard battery'

errors.claim: It had a channel wheel, preview button, and protected channel-number buttons.
errors.why_wrong: Transcript says a 'previous channel button', not a preview button.
